value.title: Apollo 15 solar-wind and electron observations
value.explanation: NASA-RP-1036 reports an approximately 3-gamma local magnetic field at the Apollo 15 site. Proton measurements showed no measurable difference from upstream solar-wind data. Electron observations were broadly similar to expected upstream values, with occasional directional particle shadowing and lunar photoelectrons in the lowest-energy channels.
value.significance: These observations characterized how the solar-wind plasma and low-energy electron population were measured at the Apollo 15 lunar surface site.

value.title: Contrasting solar-wind observations at Apollo 12 and Apollo 15
value.explanation: The 1975 comparison paper reports stronger solar-wind perturbations at Apollo 12 than at Apollo 15. The Apollo 12 site had a relatively stronger local magnetic field; Apollo 15 observations showed no noticeable differences from upstream solar-wind properties.
value.significance: The two-site comparison provided evidence that local lunar environments differed in their observed interaction with the solar wind.

value.title: Simultaneous lunar-surface plasma observations
value.explanation: The Apollo 15 SWS joined the Apollo 12 SWS as a second solar-wind spectrometer on the lunar surface. NASA SP-289 notes that the two instruments were separated by approximately 1,100 km and offered the opportunity to compare solar plasma at two locations.
value.significance: The two-site measurements supported comparisons of solar-wind plasma conditions and their interaction with the Moon.

value.title: Comparative observations of the solar wind at two lunar sites
value.explanation: The Apollo 12/Apollo 15 study compared spectrometer observations from two lunar locations and reported stronger solar-wind perturbations at Apollo 12 than at Apollo 15, alongside the difference in their local magnetic-field environments.
value.significance: The comparison helped investigate how local lunar magnetic environments relate to solar-wind plasma observations at the lunar surface.

value.title: Two-layer near-surface seismic velocity structure at the Apollo 16 Descartes site
value.explanation: Apollo 16 ASE preliminary analysis identified a 114 m/s compressional-wave velocity in the surface layer, interpreted as lunar regolith. A faster 250 m/s refracting horizon was estimated at 12.2 m depth. NASA treated the deeper material's geological identity as preliminary rather than definitively established.
value.significance: The result provided an in-situ seismic constraint on the shallow highlands subsurface and helped distinguish the regolith from the underlying material at the Descartes landing site.

value.title: Apollo 16 highlands active-seismic profile
value.explanation: The ASE added an active-seismic profile from the Descartes highlands, providing a measured near-surface velocity and evidence for a deeper, faster refracting horizon. NASA compared the 114 m/s Apollo 16 surface-layer result with earlier Apollo landing-site values; those earlier values are comparisons only, not Apollo 16 measurements.
value.significance: The experiment expanded the geographic coverage of lunar near-surface seismic measurements into a highlands setting and supported comparative studies of lunar regolith properties.

value.title: Engineering lessons from HP³ subsurface penetration attempt
value.explanation: The HP³ mole encountered regolith behaviour that did not provide sufficient friction for its self-hammering mechanism to advance to the intended depth. The mission’s attempts to assist the mole generated operational and engineering experience for future planetary subsurface systems.
value.significance: The attempt documented the challenges of penetrating Martian regolith with a self-hammering probe; the intended deep heat-flow measurement was not achieved.
